blocks.text: Paraty, Brazil: looking up at the brightly painted corner of a historic house

Start in São Paulo, a centre of business and culture, then see Iguazú Falls from both sides. After Rio, the trip takes on a quieter pace. Ilha Grande is car-free, while Paraty preserves its 18th-century streets and houses. Spend the final day near the fishing village of Trindade, with beaches, a trail through the Atlantic Forest and a visit to the natural pool at Caixa d’Aço.

## What to Expect on This Itinerary

The first half of the trip takes in major city sights and natural landmarks. São Paulo introduces you to Brazil’s business and cultural capital. Spend two days among waterfalls and tropical forest at Iguazú, then explore Rio’s historic centre and take in the city from its two main viewpoints.




The pace changes noticeably in the second half. On Ilha Grande, you get around by boat and on foot. A boat trip gives you a view of the island from the water and includes stops for swimming. Next comes Paraty, a small colonial town where historic streets sit close to the beaches and forests of the Atlantic coast.




The final day in Trindade is more active, with several beaches, a moderately challenging trail and the natural pool at Caixa d’Aço. The walk to Cachadaço Beach takes about 40 minutes. In the natural pool among the rocks, you can swim or snorkel and watch for colourful fish and other marine life. The itinerary moves from major cities and full sightseeing days to islands, the ocean and a quieter stretch of coast.
